error_reason: The Planner erroneously conflated 'Reduced Salinity Level' (RSL) with a global drop in ocean volume, leading to a misinterpretation of the primary mechanism of Permian extinction impacts. By treating meltwater-induced freshening (RSL) as evidence of sea-level recession (Option B), the agent diverted the entire search strategy away from the correct answer regarding salinity and density changes (Option A) from the very beginning.

hypotheses.rationale: The Planner incorrectly interprets a paper about 'Reduced Salinity Level' (RSL) fall as evidence of 'sea level fall' (ocean volume reduction). These are distinct geological phenomena: RSL refers to highstands (freshening) caused by meltwater influx, whereas Option B requires a global drop in ocean volume (eastering due to ice sheets). By misidentifying the mechanism from the very first analysis step, the entire multi-agent search strategy was derelieved to focus on the wrong mechanism (sea level drop) rather than checking salinity/density effects.
hypotheses.check: Verify if the content of the cited Heliyon/PMC article actually supports a global drop in ocean volume (ice storage) or if it describes 'Reduced Salinity Level' (freshening) during a marine highstand.
